correctness.rationale: The exact column-sum identity follows by discrete differences and stochastic monotonicity. Each signed row difference is the derivative of tail gaps in [0,beta]. Convex maximization on the cube bounds half its variation by floor(n/2)beta. Endpoint tail events give delta >= beta. Interlaced disjoint-support rows and uniform smoothing attain the upper factor for strictly positive kernels; smoothed identity attains the lower factor. Exact rational tests corroborate all boundaries and sharp constructions, not infinite validity.

value.rationale: Provides an optimal dimension-dependent comparison between adjacent regularity of transformed functions and global Markov oscillation contraction, with exact worst case and first-dimension barrier. Strictly positive interlaced kernels show why positivity and stochastic monotonicity alone cannot give dimension-free equivalence, a structural distinction needed for translating Markov stability bounds.
